title: Static Routing on Junos: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Imagine moving into a brand new housing estate. Your sat nav doesn't know the roads yet. So you draw the map by hand.

lines.t: Your sat nav doesn't know it

scenes.heading: The hand-drawn map
scenes.narration: A static route is a hand drawn map. You tell the router exactly where to send traffic, and it never changes unless you change it. You need a destination and a next hop. The catch-all road is the default route. If two maps disagree, the lower number wins.

scenes.heading: In Junos
scenes.narration: Here's the syntax. A static route needs a prefix and a next hop. The default route uses zero slash zero. And you can add a higher preference to make it a backup. Here's a normal static route. This is the default route. And a higher preference makes it a backup.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. A static route doesn't switch to a backup unless you configure one. The default route is the last resort, because the most specific match wins. And every static route needs a next hop.
